segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be looking after you during your surgery. Can you confirm your full name and today's date for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doctor. I'm Tan Kiah Choon, and today's 15th March. Surgery's for my gallbladder, right? They said something about stones causing pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Yes, you're scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Can you tell me more about your gallbladder issues? How long have you been having symptoms?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: About half a year already. Had bad pain after eating, especially oily food. Doctor said stones are blocking, so need to remove it lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medications. Can you confirm your current list, especially any changes to your blood pressure medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I take Amlodipine 10mg every morning for BP. Used to be on Enalapril, but stopped six months back because of the cough side effect. Now only Amlodipine, plus Metformin for diabetes, Atorvastatin for cholesterol, Levothyroxine for thyroid, and Omeprazole but stopped that already.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. So no Enalapril currently, only Amlodipine for hypertension. Any allergies we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No allergies, doctor. Never had reactions to any medicines or foods.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. You mentioned diabetes and high cholesterol – are these well-controlled with your current medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. Blood sugar and cholesterol levels are okay with the meds. BP also stable with Amlodipine.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight? We need to confirm you're NPO for surgery.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No food or water since last night, like the nurse instructed. Just a bit of water with my morning pills, but that was hours ago lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Any previous anesthesia experiences we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first surgery. Never had general anesthesia before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright. How are you managing with daily activities? Any shortness of breath or chest pain on exertion?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No issues, doctor. Can climb stairs slowly and walk to the market without problems.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. We'll be using general anesthesia with a short-acting agent, and you'll have pain relief through a PCA pump after surgery. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No questions, doctor. Just want to get this over with and feel better.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Of course. We'll take good care of you. I'll see you in the holding area before the operation.
